description: Fork-specific action provenance registry. Cherri action definitions remain the sole source of truth for parameters, plist keys, types, enums, defaults, and semantics. This registry answers exactly one question: did this behavior originate in upstream Cherri, or was it added or materially changed by this fork?

upstream.baselineSubject: Remove unnecessary identifier from file() action
upstream.baselineDetermination: merge-base(HEAD, upstream/main) when this registry was created; the fork branch contains the full upstream history, so every fork change is a descendant of this SHA.
upstream.note: Re-record a fresh baseline (new merge-base) whenever upstream is synced; never rewrite existing entries.

changeType.added-by-fork: The action does not exist in upstream Cherri at the recorded baseline; this fork introduced it.
changeType.modified-by-fork: The action exists at the recorded baseline; this fork extended or corrected its parameters, serialization, compiler handling, or decompiler handling.

upstreamStatus.absent-upstream: No such action in upstream at baseline.
upstreamStatus.present-upstream-extended: Present upstream; fork added capability without changing existing behavior.
upstreamStatus.present-upstream-corrected: Present upstream; fork changed existing behavior to fix incorrect output.

conventions.noEntryMeans: Inherited from upstream and untouched by this fork. Do not create entries for unchanged actions.
conventions.supersededByUpstream: Set to the upstream SHA/subject that later provided equivalent functionality natively. Keep the entry and append to history instead of deleting it, then decide whether to drop, keep, or reconcile the fork implementation.
conventions.firstForkCommit: The fork commit that INTRODUCED the change. Never the commit that records the metadata itself. See workflow below.

nonCircularProvenance: 1. Implement and test the action/infrastructure change.
2. Commit the implementation. This produces a stable implementation SHA.
3. In a SEPARATE follow-up commit, record firstForkCommit values referencing that implementation SHA (batch several entries into one provenance-metadata commit if practical).
4. Validate referenced SHAs (TestForkActionProvenanceRegistry does this when .git is present), then push both commits.
5. Never amend an already-referenced implementation commit: doing so invalidates every recorded SHA pointing at it.
6. If an implementation commit must be rewritten for safety reasons, update all referencing entries in the next provenance-metadata commit.
workflow.whySeparateCommits: A commit cannot contain its own final SHA: editing the registry inside the implementation commit would change that commit's hash. The registry therefore always points one commit backwards, which is stable.

recovery.restoreUpstreamBehavior: git show <baselineSha>:<upstreamLocation> > <forkLocation> (then re-run tests); prefer re-implementing over blind restore when later fork changes depend on it.

seededFrom: batch-001 corpus analysis (analysis/batch-001). Historical audit against baseline 951c0bb found no pre-existing fork-specific action changes; all earlier fork divergence was iOS app, skill, CI, docs, tooling, and the action catalog generator itself.

actions.name: runJavaScriptOnWebpage
actions.change: Added optional input parameter (&variable ?input: 'WFInput') so compiled actions can carry the webpage-content input real Shortcuts serialize.
actions.reason: Every observed real-world sample carried WFInput; upstream definition emitted WFJavaScript only.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001: OBSERVED x4 (4 independent shapes), analysis/batch-001/variants.json (pre-fix)

actions.name: saveFile
actions.change: Added optional folder reference parameter (&variable ?folder: 'WFFolder') alongside the legacy path-based destination.
actions.reason: Modern Shortcuts serialize Save File with WFFolder {displayName,fileLocation,filename} next to WFFileDestinationPath and WFAskWhereToSave; legacy path behavior preserved.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001: OBSERVED x3 shapes carrying WFFolder + WFAskWhereToSave
notes: Observed WFFolder payload is an Apple-side picker structure; Cherri emits a variable reference attachment instead. Structural equivalence unverified on-device.

actions.name: openApp
actions.change: Added optional slideOver bool parameter (WFOpenInSlideOver) and matching custom-decompiler argument emission; made replaceAppIDs skip non-string arguments so boolean parameters coexist with app ID replacement.
actions.reason: Real samples carry WFOpenInSlideOver:true (x2) and fuller WFSelectedApp dicts; slide-over was unrepresentable.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001: OBSERVED x6 shapes; WFOpenInSlideOver x2; round-trip verified via tests/corpus-batch001.cherri
notes: WFSelectedApp Name/TeamIdentifier enrichment intentionally NOT implemented: no local source for those values; inventing them would violate evidence rules.
replaceAppIDs hardening is required collateral of the new parameter type.

actions.name: run
actions.change: Moved run() from declarative DSL (actions/shortcuts.cherri, definition removed) to a builtin in actions_std.go so compilation emits the modern WFWorkflow reference dict {workflowIdentifier,isSelf:false,workflowName} together with the legacy WFWorkflowName key, mirroring the existing runSelf pattern; added decompiler support emitting both arguments.
actions.reason: Real Shortcuts carry the dict form next to the legacy name key; improves emitted fidelity and structural round-trip while preserving the one-line UX.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001: OBSERVED x3 shapes containing WFWorkflow dict; verified round-trip via tests/shortcuts.cherri
notes: workflowIdentifier is a generated placeholder UUID because name-to-UUID resolution requires device data; Shortcuts resolves through workflowName. This derivation is INFERRED from existing runSelf behavior, not confirmed on-device.

Follow-up decompiler correction (same session as the App Intent descriptor generalization): run() now quotes plain WFWorkflowName literals on decompile and the run/runSelf post-check syncs the definition with the resolved name, so run targets survive round-trip instead of decompiling to run().
history: Follow-up correction: decompiled run() keeps its quoted shortcutName argument; run/runSelf descriptor check no longer leaves a mismatched definition after split matching.

actions.name: conditional
actions.upstreamLocation: compiler construct (parser.go collectConditionals, shortcutgen.go makeConditionalAction, decompile.go decompConditional)
actions.change: Added optional `legacy` keyword in if statements (`if legacy <conditions> {`). When present, compilation emits WFConditionalLegacyComparisonBehavior:true on the conditional start action; the decompiler reconstructs the keyword when the flag is present. Output is unchanged unless the keyword is used. Catalog compilerConstruct emittedKeys extended accordingly.
actions.reason: Real modern Shortcuts re-saving conditionals emit WFConditionalLegacyComparisonBehavior; without the keyword the flag was unrepresentable and round-trip lossy.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001 x2 + shortcut-lib decoded samples x3 (5 observations, 2 independent sources, clients 3612/4033)
notes: Keyword placement before the condition list avoids ambiguity with !x has-value forms and && chains.
Observed evidence covers single-comparison form; multi-condition predicate-form emission shares the same key placement.

Follow-up correction (same session as the App Intent descriptor generalization): WFCondition is now always emitted on predicate templates. LessThan serializes as 0 and the previous omitempty tag silently dropped the operator from &&-chain templates, which also crashed decompilation of those exports.
history: Follow-up correction: predicate templates always emit WFCondition (LessThan=0 no longer omitted); decompCondition treats absence as LessThan for older exports instead of panicking. Recorded with the infrastructure entry 'app intent descriptor generalization'.

actions.name: base64Encode / base64Decode
actions.change: Added optional trailing text parameter lineBreakMode ('WFBase64LineBreakMode') to both base64Encode and base64Decode; omitted when not provided. Documented values: 'None' (observed in real modern export), 'Every 64 Characters', 'Every 76 Characters' (ToolKit v78 corroboration); value domain intentionally left incomplete, modeled as pass-through text.
actions.reason: Real Shortcuts serialize the line-break mode next to WFInput/WFEncodeMode; previously unrepresentable.
actions.evidence: local batch-001 x1 (client 3612, 'None') + playground golden x1 (historical client, 'None'); ToolKit v78 enum cases corroborate domain
notes: Required a decompiler split-action matching fix: static DSL appendParams maps were never scored, so encode/decode names sharing the identifier tied once both declared the parameter and the winner was iteration-order dependent. Static maps now score like appendParamsFunc-derived params (see infrastructure entry).

actions.name: getUpcomingEvents
actions.change: New declarative action getUpcomingEvents(number ?count: 'WFGetUpcomingItemCount', text ?dateSpecifier: 'WFDateSpecifier', text ?specifiedDate: 'WFSpecifiedDate'): variable. All parameters optional; omitted keys are not emitted. Output type variable (container reader pattern).
actions.reason: Action absent from upstream; corpus evidence matured to two independent real corpora with an empty-parameter shape proving optionality of every key.
actions.evidence: corpus batch-001 x1 (full shape incl. WFSpecifiedDate) + shortcut-lib x2 (full + empty shapes); dateSpecifier values 'Today' and 'Specified Day' observed across both sources
notes: WFGetUpcomingItemCalendar intentionally NOT implemented: payload embeds device-generated picker data (calendar UUID, RGBAValue, localized title) that cannot be reproduced from source alone. Calendar-carrying export shapes therefore classify VARIANT until a representation is designed; minimal shapes compile KNOWN.
dateSpecifier is free text, not an enum: only 'Today'/'Specified Day' observed; full domain unverified.
specifiedDate observed as locale-formatted date string.
